answer: Admission is capped at 3 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm as a result spreads across origins and pays for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the violet quota and the canyon admission check. Because the falcon audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 26 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
